_comment: South Africa's jurisdiction table. Authority NAMES are real and public; every
EMAIL here is a non-routable placeholder on the reserved .invalid TLD, on
purpose, so that a misconfigured run cannot reach a real regulator. Real
addresses belong in authorities.za.json, which overrides this file and is not
committed.
Keys are province and city names as reverse geocoding returns them; case and
accents are folded on both sides.
The law is the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004
(NEM:AQA). Section 36 makes metropolitan and district municipalities the
licensing authorities for listed activities, which is why an industrial
emission resolves to a metro or a district rather than to the province. On the
Mpumalanga Highveld, Nkangala District licenses the power stations and mines in
Emalahleni and Steve Tshwete, and Gert Sibande District licenses those in Govan
Mbeki (Secunda), Lekwa and Msukaligwa. Sources: the National Air Quality
Officer's 2023 and 2024 reports on saaqis.environment.gov.za, and Eskom's
atmospheric emission licence register.
Provincial department names are from each province's 2026/27 budget vote at
treasury.gov.za. Gauteng's environment function became a standalone
Department of Environment in 2024.
No South African statute sets a deadline for answering an air pollution
complaint, so every response_window_days is null and the lookup uses
follow_up_days instead, marked as not statutory.
local_language is the language spoken most often in households in that
province, from Census 2022 (Stats SA P0301.4, table 2.9). It is the language a
summary for residents is written in, not the language of the complaint, which
is English.

industrial_emission.statute: National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004
industrial_emission.section: Section 22, no listed activity without an atmospheric emission licence, and section 51, offences including breach of licence conditions; section 36 names the licensing authority
industrial_emission.response_window_note: The Air Quality Act sets no deadline for a licensing authority to answer a complaint. The interval shown is this system's suggested follow-up, not a statutory period.

open_waste_burning.section: Section 28, duty of care to prevent significant pollution
open_waste_burning.response_window_note: No statute sets a deadline for a municipality to answer a pollution complaint. The interval shown is this system's suggested follow-up, not a statutory period.

crop_residue_burning.section: Section 28, duty of care to prevent significant pollution
crop_residue_burning.response_window_note: No statute sets a deadline for a provincial department to answer a pollution complaint. The interval shown is this system's suggested follow-up, not a statutory period.
